do_while_loop.quote: Zero times; 10 < 5 is false; so the loop never starts
do_while_loop.rule: wrong rule: A do-while whose condition starts false runs its body zero times. Right rule: The first test is omitted: the body always runs at least once, and the condition is checked only after each pass.

paths.label: held
paths.quote: Zero times; 10 < 5 is false; so the loop never starts
paths.logic: A do-while whose condition starts false runs its body zero times.
paths.twin_logic: The statements within the do block are always executed at least once.

paths.label: correct
paths.quote: Zero times; 10 < 5 is false; so the loop never starts
paths.logic: The loop body always runs at least once, even if the condition is false at the start.
paths.twin_logic: A while or for body runs zero times when the condition is false at the start.

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: Zero times; 10 < 5 is false; so the loop never starts
paths.logic: Applies the LT rule unevenly: on a trace, the condition is tested before the first pass on some runs (as for while) and after it on others, or one more pass is run after the condition becomes false. The traced number of passes is off by one. (here mixing in: "A do-while whose condition starts false runs its body zero times")

paths.label: broken
paths.quote: Zero times; 10 < 5 is false; so the loop never starts
paths.logic: A do-while loop has the same control parts as a while loop (the variable set before, the condition, the update in the body); only the test is moved after the body.

paths.label: broken
paths.quote: Zero times; so the loop never starts
paths.logic: The block between do and while is the loop body; it runs first and is repeated while the condition holds.

paths.label: confirmed
paths.logic: The init, condition and update all act on the loop variable: the init sets it, the condition tests it, the update changes it.

paths.label: shown
paths.quote: 10 < 5 is false; so the loop never starts
paths.logic: The loop variable is set once by the initialization, tested by the continuation condition before each pass and updated (usually incremented) at the end of each pass; declared in a for header, it is not available after the loop.

paths.label: shown
paths.logic: One update changes only the loop variable (i = i + 1 turns 4 into 5); one test reads it and yields true or false; an assignment to it in the body changes what the next test sees.

evidence.label: shown
evidence.quote: Zero times; 10 < 5 is false; so the loop never starts
evidence.logic: Folk meaning: in English 'do X while Y' means do X during the time that Y holds, with Y watched continuously, as in the 'while demon'. In Java the condition is tested only at the bottom, after each complete pass of the body, and the first pass always runs.
